# Hydropower consumption. Data by Countries from 1965 to 2025

Authorization is required. Log In

 Statistical Review of World Energy BP bp.com 

 Energy institute energyinst.org 

 | Overview (Sep 21, 2026) 

 Global primary hydropower consumption in 2025 amounted to 16.12 EJ, 0.13% higher than in 2024. Since 2000, the indicator has increased by 69.24%. Hydropower accounted for 2.68% of total global primary energy consumption in 2025, compared with 2.50% in 2000. 

 China remained the leader at 5.01 EJ (+2.08% y/y; 31.09% of the global total). It was followed by Brazil at 1.43 EJ (-5.67%; 8.88% share) and Canada at 1.25 EJ (+0.45%; 7.78% share). Rounding out the TOP-5 were the United States at 0.88 EJ (+1.97%) and Russia at 0.72 EJ (-5.03%). Among the fastest-growing consumers over the past year were Colombia (+24.99%), Ecuador (+24.36%), Mexico (+21.84%), Indonesia (+16.75%), Vietnam (+14.78%) and India (+13.74%). Since 2000, the strongest percentage increases in hydropower consumption were recorded by Vietnam (+599.90%), China (+525.80%), Indonesia (+217.80%), Pakistan (+127.70%), India (+131.47%), as well as Colombia (+121.12%) and Peru (+110.19%). 

 Europe. The top three were Russia at 0.72 EJ (-5.03%), Norway at 0.52 EJ (+4.02%), and Sweden at 0.25 EJ (+5.90%). The regional picture is shaped by stable hydropower consumption in Scandinavia alongside declines in France (-18.16%) and Italy (-22.04%) in 2025, highlighting the sensitivity of Southern Europe to hydrological conditions. 

 Asia. The leaders were China at 5.01 EJ (+2.08%), India at 0.64 EJ (+13.74%) and Vietnam at 0.37 EJ (+14.78%). The trend is driven by long-term capacity expansion in China and accelerating growth in India and Vietnam, while Japan (-6.58%) and Turkey (-23.29%) reduced hydropower consumption in 2025. 

 North and Latin America. The top three were Brazil at 1.43 EJ (-5.67%), Canada at 1.25 EJ (+0.45%), and the United States at 0.88 EJ (+1.97%). Against the backdrop of a decline in Brazil, a notable recovery was recorded in the Andean countries: Colombia (+24.99%), Peru (+6.12%), and Ecuador (+24.36%), along with growth in Mexico (+21.84%). 

 Africa. The top three by volume were Egypt at 0.05 EJ (-4.00%), South Africa at 0.0065 EJ (+67.05%), and Morocco at 0.0015 EJ (+25.64%). In absolute terms, the region remains a small consumer, although 2025 brought notable growth in South Africa and Morocco from a low base, while North Africa, represented by Egypt, saw a slight decline. 

 Globally, hydropower consumption in 2025 was almost unchanged from 2024, while its share in the energy mix increased compared with the beginning of the century. Structurally, the center of gravity is shifting toward Asia, driven by China and accelerating hydropower consumption in India and Vietnam, while results in Latin America were mixed: a decline in Brazil was offset by growth in Colombia, Peru and Ecuador. The 2025 balance reflects the impact of hydrological volatility and new capacity additions in Asia, while further global growth potential depends on the investment cycle in dams and water availability in key river basins.
